extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants for EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships (post-PhD researchers seeking postdoctoral funding)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection criteria for applicants seeking EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships, covering the evaluation dimensions (candidate, project, host), application components, interview expectations, discouraged applications, and bias considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence of the candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary selection criterion: scientific excellence of the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What makes a strong candidate: excellent PhD productivity; strong publications (preferably first author in respected journals); personal initiative and impact; clear research vision. Career interruptions are considered fairly. EMBO is a DORA signatory and does not rely on journal impact factors as the sole metric; assess quality of contributions over quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence of the project
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary selection criterion: scientific excellence of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong projects are original and ambitious, have a well-defined hypothesis, sound methodology, are clearly differentiated from the applicant's PhD work, and are feasible within the fellowship duration. Projects that are a continuation of an applicant's PhD research will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence of the host laboratory
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary selection criterion: scientific excellence of the host laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong host is a renowned international research group, provides new techniques/approaches relative to the applicant's PhD lab, has a strong record of training, and provides a letter of acceptance with a detailed plan. Applications to work with host laboratories with which the candidate has collaborated in the past generally receive lower priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-screening application components
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 pre-screening evaluates a condensed application form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials reviewed include: summary of the applicant's main scientific achievements; three most important publications; summary and biological significance of the proposed work; justification for choice of the host lab; reference and acceptance letters. About twice the number of available fellowships are selected for interview (~25% pass pre-screening).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview performance (scientific depth, presentation, defence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 2 interview assesses the applicant beyond the written materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews are remote (videoconferencing), last 90 minutes, and are conducted by an interviewer with expertise in the application area (selected from EMBO Members and EMBO Young Investigators). The interview tests scientific depth, presentation, and the ability to defend the project. The applicant is responsible for contacting the interviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final independent evaluation by committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 3 final selection is made by independent evaluation of the full application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications selected to the 2nd stage are independently evaluated by five members of the EMBO Fellowship Committee; each member evaluates the full application. Consensus or a vote determines the final list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouraged application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Application types that receive lower priority or are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications to work with host laboratories with which the candidate has collaborated in the past generally receive lower priority. Projects that are a continuation of an applicant's PhD research will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation of mobility after PhD as part of eligibility/value judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a strong emphasis on changing host institution after the PhD; cross-country and cross-continent moves are particularly valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation bias and metrics policy (DORA compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles governing fair evaluation and use of metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO is a DORA signatory: evaluators should not rely on journal impact factors as the sole metric. Emphasis is on the quality of contributions over quantity. Career interruptions are explicitly considered fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline / decision timeframe
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The outcome of the selection is known between 16 to 18 weeks after the evaluation deadline.
